And the Caliph laughed,
and ordered for him robes and much gold.
And after him arose his son Gabriel, the son of Bukhtishu, son {OCR?} of George, the son of Bukhtishu.
And he too became distinguished in the medical art,
and served Harun al-Rashid.
And it is related
that one day one of the maidservants who was beloved by the Caliph stretched herself,
and when she raised her arm, it became stiff,
and she was no longer able to bend it.
And the physicians grew weary from the multitude of ointments and bandages that they applied to her,
and they did not benefit her at all.
Then the Caliph summoned Gabriel
and related her case to him.
And he said,
"I have a cure for her, if you bring her out here before the assembly,
and I do to her whatever I wish,
and you do not become angry with me."
And the Caliph agreed,
and they brought her out.
And as soon as Gabriel saw her, he ran toward her,
and seized her skirts as though wishing to uncover her nakedness.
Then that girl, out of the greatness of her shame, her body grew hot and she sweated,
and her limbs relaxed,
and she stretched out her arm—
which had been suspended aloft—
toward her skirts and grasped them,
while covering herself.
And immediately that Gabriel left her, and said to the Caliph,
"Behold, she is cured henceforth."
And that young woman stretched out her arm to the right and to the left.
And the Caliph and all those present were astonished,
and he ordered for him five hundred thousand white [coins] (dirhams).
And when he stood up,
he asked him about the cause.
He said,
"A certain thin humor poured into this woman's limbs at the time of intercourse,
and because that motion of coitus suddenly ceased and rested,
that humor thickened in the pores of the nerves that move the arm,
and nothing could dissolve it
except heat with inflammation arising from violent motion such as that."
And his annual stipends amounted to nine hundred thousand dinars.
And when Rashid died,
he served al-Amin, his son.
And when al-Amin was killed,
he served al-Mamun, his brother.
At first, Mamun {OCR?} was angry with him,
and plundered all his property.
Afterwards he was reconciled and returned everything that he had taken from him,
and loved him and honored him.
